session_scope: SFP DOM/vendor fields on RouterOS x86: reference research + static userland trace. Read-only research; no firmware build, no device access, no key/tag/asset changes.
owner_request: Make x86 show SFP attenuation/DOM and vendor fields like CCR; search references and modify the NPK (existing notes: docs/sfp-bcm57800-npk-feasibility.md).

mikrotik_iso.downloaded_via: curl http1.1 resume (two attempts; transfer interrupted once at 42%)

system_npk.note: Byte-identical to the pinned qualified source NPK in patch.py (_X86_INSTALLER_SOURCE_SHA256) and to docs/sfp-driver-findings.md 'vendor.npk'.

inputs.extraction: unsquashfs -cat per file (full-tree extraction stops on APFS case collision xt_DSCP.ko/xt_dscp.ko, same as HANDOFF §7). Files traced: nova/bin/* (78 binaries), bnx2x.ko.

references_found.finding: Bare-metal ROS v7 x86 (Supermicro, Intel 82599ES + X710 SFP+): SFP diagnostics/vendor info absent from /interface ethernet monitor; reporter states it worked in ROS v6; no official MikroTik statement; unresolved as of 7.14.2.
SNMP optical Tx/Rx via MIKROTIK-MIB ifOpticalTable discussion; availability depends on the DDM data being present at all.
Community GPL source mirror (2024-03-19 expansion) for MikroTik kernel-side drivers; not used to build anything in this session.

static_trace_method: Custom Capstone i386 ELF32 analysis (repo venv, capstone 5.0.7): parse sections/dynsym/rel.plt, resolve ioctl PLT, enumerate raw 0x8946 (SIOCETHTOOL) dword sites in .text, disassemble windows, catalogue ethtool cmd immediates; regex byte-scan for mov-imm/push of 0x42/0x43; .rodata dword scan with neighbor check; string scan for genl family names and sysfs paths.

findings.only_net_uses_ethtool: Of 78 nova/bin binaries, only 'net' contains SIOCETHTOOL dwords (12) and the string 'ethtool' (1 hit: 'ETH: failed SLINKSETTINGS ethtool').
findings.module_eeprom_cmds_absent: Zero constructions of ETHTOOL_GMODULEINFO (0x42) or ETHTOOL_GMODULEEEPROM (0x43): no mov-imm/push in .text, no plausible .rodata command table containing them (raw 0x42 dwords sit inside ASCII strings), and no generic-netlink 'ethtool' family usage.
findings.driver_side_present: Vendor bnx2x.ko (kernel 5.6.3-64) still exports bnx2x_read_sfp_module_eeprom; docs/sfp-driver-findings.md previously documented its ethtool ops table callbacks incl. A0/A2 paths.
findings.sysfs_private_surface_in_net: Only MikroTik-private sysfs path found: /sys/devices/virtual/net/%s/ros_%sprbs (plus standard /sys/class/net/ scanning).

conclusion: RouterOS 7.24.4 x86 userland never issues the ioctl commands that read SFP module identity/DDM EEPROM. Therefore vendor/part-number and rx/tx-power fields cannot appear in /interface ethernet monitor on x86 for ANY NIC driven by standard Linux drivers (including BCM57800/bnx2x), regardless of module DDM support. Replacing or rebuilding bnx2x.ko cannot fix this: the driver-side reader exists but nothing in userland calls it. This independently corroborates the public v6-to-v7 x86 regression reports.
ccr_parity_boundary: How MikroTik's own boards deliver SFP data to net (likely a private driver-to-userland channel; a '..include/umsg/netlink.h' debug string exists in net) was NOT verified in this session - requires non-x86 system NPK binaries or GPL driver source analysis. The x86-side negative above is the decision-relevant fact for this request.
why_no_npk_modification_was_implemented: The requested 'modify the NPK so x86 equals CCR' is not a container/repack change: it would require injecting a new feature (GMODULEINFO/GMODULEEEPROM query + SFF-8072/8472 decode + calibration + monitor property publication + console schema) into the closed, stripped, 32-bit nova/bin/net ELF, re-done per RouterOS release, and unverifiable without owner hardware. Not attempted per repo rules against speculative unevidenced patches.
limits: Static analysis of one x86 7.24.4 build (hashes above); not a runtime test on the owner's machine.
Negative searches prove absence in the scanned code/data surfaces, not absence of every conceivable dynamically-computed path.
No ethtool -m / EEPROM read attempted anywhere (bnx2x Warpcore retry can power-cycle a module; see sfp-bcm57800-npk-feasibility.md).
Scratch artifacts (ISO/NPK/extracts) live in /tmp/ali-sfp-research and may vanish; this JSON plus recorded hashes is the durable record.
No test suite run: no production code changed in this session.
sanitization: No key material, Software/System IDs, MACs, or license blocks are present in this record.

addendum_2026_10_08_b3_verdict_and_route.b3_agent_verdict: packet_hook.ko's netlink-27 input callback is ONLY a raw frame injector ({ifindex,meta,frame} -> dev_queue_xmit; unknown ifindex -> printk drop). No message parsing, no 0xA0B1/magic constants anywhere in the module, no netlink_unicast reply path. packet_hook also creates units 26/29/30 with NULL input. Conclusion: the RPC 0xA0B1 responder is NOT packet_hook.
addendum_2026_10_08_b3_verdict_and_route.userland_magic_census: Of all 78 nova/bin binaries, only net itself contains the RPC magics (B0A000B0/11223344/A0B1). parser has one coincidental 0xA0B1 dword. sys2/www/keyman: zero. So no evident userspace peer validates the magic; if a peer exists it parses by structure (unproven).
addendum_2026_10_08_b3_verdict_and_route.bind_connect_census: net binds multiple netlink sockets with sockaddr_nl(family=0x10) incl. groups=0xffffffff (sniffer mirrors); the RPC socket is connected (send() with 4 args); exact dst portid of the bus socket not yet extracted (helper 0x8053120 wraps bind/connect).
addendum_2026_10_08_b3_verdict_and_route.route_decision_for_cli_dom: Given (a) no kernel responder machinery exists on x86, (b) no userspace responder identifiable, (c) vendor bnx2x/ixgbe drivers ALREADY implement standard ethtool module-EEPROM readers, and (d) the friend's build is version-locked (strong hint of a per-build binary patch): the primary route to CLI DOM parity is PATCHING nova/bin/net per build (7.24.4 and 7.24.5 both in hand) to populate the existing sfp-* monitor properties from standard ETHTOOL_GMODULEINFO/GMODULEEEPROM ioctls it already knows how to issue. This requires no kernel module build and matches the friend's version-lock behavior. The previously-considered kernel-responder route is deprioritized (a second input callback on unit 27 is impossible; packet_hook is the owner).
next_steps: Map net's sfp property-fill cluster precisely (anchors: initQsfp ~0x80746xx, property IDs 0x3FB/0x3FC/0x1002E, onReadModule 0x806dffe) and design the smallest patch: gate + GMODULEINFO/GMODULEEEPROM queries + fill.
Prototype on 7.24.4 first (same binary as lab), verify in QEMU semantics via code-path reasoning, then on hardware with an optical DOM module (QEMU cannot emulate SFP EEPROM).

addendum_2026_10_08_b2_packet_hook_inter.trigger: Workstream B2 on both 7.24.4 and 7.24.5 (same kernel 5.6.3-64, same protocol surface).
addendum_2026_10_08_b2_packet_hook_inter.netlink_registry_found_in_gpl: The GPL patch adds MikroTik's custom netlink protocol registry to include/uapi/linux/netlink.h: NETLINK_WIRELESS=17, NETLINK_STP=23, NETLINK_UNICL=24, NETLINK_MESH=25, NETLINK_LOG=26, NETLINK_PACKET_HOOK=27, NETLINK_LTE_GCT=28, NETLINK_ADDRLIST=29, NETLINK_PTP_HOOK=30. This CONFIRMS protocol 27 = NETLINK_PACKET_HOOK (the bus net uses), owned by packet_hook.ko. packet_hook.c source is NOT in the GPL dump (binary-only module) and 0xA0B1 appears nowhere in the patch.
packet_hook_symtab_facts: Module is unstripped (full .symtab). proto_handlers = STT_OBJECT at .text offset 0x1300, size 2104 bytes = 263 x 8-byte list heads.
register_proto (58 bytes @0x89b0) = linked-list head-insert into proto_handlers[slot]; node layout {ptr@0, next@8}. unregister_proto analogous.

Import census across all 298 vendor .ko: NO module imports register_proto/proto_handlers. Importers use fast-path/rx/tx/skb-bin APIs only (atl1c, bridge2, dot1x, fp_usbnet, l2tp, mbim, mesh, mpls_fp, pppoefp, pptp, romon, switch, traffic_gen, vmxnet3, vxlan2, xt_layer7, xt_misc, c2).
fast_path_register_ipproto/unregister_ipproto reference proto_handlers -> that table serves the fastpath IP-protocol family; it is NOT (yet proven to be) the RPC message dispatch.

netlink input callback and message routing (how an incoming NETLINK_PACKET_HOOK datagram reaches a responder, incl. msg 0xA0B1) not yet located: many static functions lack st_size, so offset->function mapping needs relocation-aware disassembly. Candidate reference cluster at .text 0x13a24/0x13f81/0x1409b.
addendum_2026_10_08_b2_packet_hook_inter.hypothesis_after_b2: Either packet_hook's netlink input handler routes messages to in-module subsystems only, or the SFP responder registers by a different mechanism (direct symbol reference from MikroTik's binary NIC drivers, or dispatch via /dev/util ioctls). The 0x89F0/0x89F1 module-type path via nv::ifreqDataIoctl remains driver-facing .ndo_do_ioctl and is implementable regardless.
next_b2_steps: Relocation-aware disassembly of packet_hook.ko: from util_init (.init.text) find the netlink_kernel_cfg.input callback; disassemble it end-to-end; identify message parse (magic 0xB0A000B0/0x52/0x11223344 check), routing key, and reply path (netlink_unicast).
Determine what answers 0xA0B1 on MikroTik's own boards: if in-module, enumerate which subsystem; if per-netdev handler table, find the registration export consumed by their NIC drivers.
Then prototype ixgbe/bnx2x handler (0x89F0 module type + 0xA0B1 EEPROM pages via the discovered mechanism).

addendum_2026_10_08_b1_transport_resolve.trigger: Agent B2 (transport trace) hit an account usage limit before completing; parent completed the trace manually with targeted probes.
chain_verified_in_net_7244: Request-builder 0x806df7c -> RPC registry 0x806dd04 (pending-callback tree, callback onReadModule @0x806dffe) -> tail-jump 0x806db22 (real sender).
Sender builds a datagram on the stack (default dst 0x52B000/0x100 at ctx+0x8c, source from ctx, marker 0xE188, payload copied via rep movsb) and calls PLT send(fd=ctx+0xc, buf, len+0x16, 0).

The bus fd is created by socket(AF_NETLINK=0x10, SOCK_RAW=3, protocol=0x1B=27) at 0x806fb2b-0x806fb32 (twin site 0x8074ad6 args identical) - MikroTik's custom netlink protocol (the 'umsg netlink' debug string).
net also opens /dev/util O_RDWR at 0x806c22f (fd at ctx+0xec) - control device of the same subsystem.
addendum_2026_10_08_b1_transport_resolve.responder_identified: packet_hook.ko is the kernel side of the bus: the ONLY vendor module containing __netlink_kernel_create + netlink_kernel_release + netlink_broadcast (registers the custom netlink protocol handler) AND util_init/util_exit (creates /dev/util). It also EXPORTS a driver-facing registration API: register_proto/unregister_proto/proto_handlers, register_rx_handler/unregister_rx_handler (+ignorefastpath variants), register_tx_handler, register_nfct_offload_handler, register_fast_path, register_gre(6)_proto, log_message, packet_hook_send, and more (54 exports total).
addendum_2026_10_08_b1_transport_resolve.workstream_b_implication: The SFP driver implementation path is now concrete: (a) answer private ioctl 0x89F0 module-type via standard .ndo_do_ioctl in ixgbe/bnx2x; (b) serve RPC 0xA0B1 module reads by registering through packet_hook's exported handler API (exact registration/dispatch semantics = next reverse step: disassemble packet_hook.ko's netlink input dispatch and register_proto), reading SFF EEPROM via the drivers' existing readers.
addendum_2026_10_08_b1_transport_resolve.limits: Static analysis; register_proto semantics not yet proven to cover message-id handlers (name suggests protocol handlers - the dispatch table layout needs the next pass). packet_hook.ko ships only in vendor trees (present in system NPK); its module is signed vendor - our rebuilt driver modules will load alongside it unchanged.

addendum_2026_10_08_gpl_source_and_priva.private_ioctl_channel_discovery: Full ioctl-range immediate scan of nova/bin/net (x86 7.24.4 AND arm 7.24.4) reveals a private SIOCDEVPRIVATE family issued by userland on BOTH architectures with matching counts: 0x89F0 (2x), 0x89F1 (6x), 0x89F2/0x89F3 (4-5x), 0x89F5 (2-5x), 0x89F6 (3x), 0x89F8 (1x), 0x89F9 (1-3x), 0x89FA (4x), 0x89FB/0x89FC (1-2x), 0x89FE (4x); plus SIOCGMIIPHY/SIOCGMIIREG (1x each). Two 0x89F0/0x89F1 sites sit inside the SFP function cluster (x86 ~0x8074f72/0x8074fc2): net builds an ifreq-like struct via helper, calls ioctl wrapper with request in ECX, stores results into per-interface struct at +0xd4/+0xd8, uses -1 as failure sentinel and clears a gate byte. Other private-ioctl sites cluster around 0x8093xxx-0x8097xxx adjacent to SFP property publication.
addendum_2026_10_08_gpl_source_and_priva.conclusion: MikroTik's driver-to-userland channel for NIC-private data (incl. SFP DOM) is the SIOCDEVPRIVATE 0x89F0-0x89FE family. Handlers exist only in MikroTik's own (binary, not-in-GPL-dump) NIC drivers; vanilla ixgbe/bnx2x route .ndo_do_ioctl to standard handlers only. Therefore native SFP DOM on x86 WITHOUT option.npk = implement the private protocol in ixgbe (X520) / bnx2x (BCM57800), sourcing data from their existing SFF EEPROM readers, shipping the rebuilt .ko inside the system NPK. This is kernel-version-locked, matching the friend's reportedly 7.23.1-only success.

addendum_2026_10_08_arm_userland_and_dri.trigger: Owner seeks a method other than option.npk to surface SFP module identity and tx/rx on x86 (NICs: Broadcom BCM57800, and friend reportedly Intel X520 on 7.23.1).

addendum_2026_10_08_arm_userland_and_dri.arm_result: Same architecture as x86: 'SIOCETHTOOL ioctl failed' and 'ETH: failed SLINKSETTINGS ethtool' strings present; exactly 12 SIOCETHTOOL construction sites (ARM MOVW r2,#0x8946, 4-byte aligned, window-decoded due to literal pools). Per-site immediate catalogue: GSET/GDRVINFO/GCOALESCE/SCOALESCE/GLINKSETTINGS/GPRIVFLAGS/0x50/0x51. ZERO sites construct GMODULEINFO(0x42)/GMODULEEEPROM(0x43). No raw 0x00008946 data dwords (constants built via MOVW).
addendum_2026_10_08_arm_userland_and_dri.conclusion_architecture: RouterOS userland (net) on BOTH x86 and ARM never pulls SFP module EEPROM via ethtool, yet MikroTik boards display DOM. Therefore SFP data is supplied kernel-side by MikroTik's own drivers through a private channel into net's internal SFP structures (initQsfp cluster; sysfs 'ros_*' pattern e.g. ros_%sprbs demonstrates dynamic private interfaces; full feed mechanism not yet identified). Consequence: a sufficient native-DOM route on x86 without option.npk is a DRIVER-level modification - add the MikroTik SFP feed to ixgbe (Intel X520) / bnx2x (BCM57800) using the GPL kernel source as reference, ship the rebuilt .ko inside the system NPK (no new package entry). This also fits the friend's reportedly version-locked success ('only 7.23.1'): kernel-module builds are version/ABI-locked.
